questions.stem: Operators must be alerted when any meter's reading in an eventstream goes above a threshold. What should you use?

options.text: A Dataflow Gen2
A deployment pipeline
A warehouse view
Activator

questions.explanation: Activator watches data such as eventstreams and takes actions, such as sending an alert, when a condition is met.

questions.stem: At Fernway, nobody is told when the nightly pipeline fails. What is the simplest fix inside the pipeline?

options.text: Add an Office 365 Outlook or Teams activity connected Upon failure to each activity that can fail
Turn off retries
Schedule the pipeline twice
Add a Wait activity

questions.explanation: A notification activity connected Upon failure runs when that activity fails. Use one per monitored activity, because an activity wired to several only fires when all of them fail.

questions.stem: A manager wants an email when a measure in a Power BI report visual drops below a target. What can they do?

options.text: Set an alert on the visual, which creates an Activator rule
Export the visual to Excel each day
Add a sensitivity label
Ask for a new pipeline

questions.explanation: Power BI visuals can create Activator alerts that watch the value and send an email or Teams message.

questions.stem: Which three actions can an Activator rule take when its condition is met? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: Send an email
Change the capacity SKU
Send a Teams message
Delete the workspace
Run a Fabric item, such as a pipeline or notebook

questions.explanation: Activator can notify people by email or Teams and can start Fabric items such as pipelines and notebooks.

questions.stem: You created an Activator rule that should send a Teams message when a temperature goes above 30. Hours later, no message has been sent, even though readings above 30 arrived. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: Rules are created in a Stopped state and you didn't select Save and start
The rule needs a Power Automate flow before it can send Teams messages
Teams actions only fire once per day
Activator only evaluates rules when a Power BI report is opened

questions.explanation: New rules start Stopped and aren't evaluated until you select Save and start. Teams is a built-in action, and rules are evaluated continuously.

questions.stem: You start a new Activator rule at 10:00. The data already ingested at 09:00 met the rule's condition. What happens?

options.text: The rule doesn't activate on data that was already ingested, only on new data
The rule can't start until the past events are deleted
The rule fires one summary action for all past events
The rule fires once for each 09:00 event that met the condition

questions.explanation: When a rule starts, activations run against newly ingested data only; the rule doesn't activate on data that already arrived.

questions.stem: An Activator rule's email action goes to the on-call team. You select Send me a test alert to preview the message. Who receives the test?

options.text: Nobody until the rule is started
The workspace Admins
You, regardless of the recipients in the Action card
Everyone in the on-call team

questions.explanation: The test alert always goes to you, whatever the recipient field says. It needs at least one past event for which the condition is true.

questions.stem: An Activator rule `value < 5` on a sensor sends an alert for every event while the value stays low, which floods the operators. What is the recommended change?

options.text: Use a stateful condition such as DECREASES or BECOMES so the rule fires on the transition
Add a second identical rule with an OR condition
Send the alert to a Teams channel instead of email
Raise the threshold to 50 so that fewer events match

questions.explanation: Stateless filters evaluate each event alone and can be noisy; stateful conditions like DECREASES or BECOMES fire on transitions and reduce spam. Changing the channel or threshold doesn't fix the repeat firing.

questions.stem: Operators must be alerted when a device that normally sends readings every minute stops sending data altogether. Which kind of Activator condition supports this?

options.text: A Power BI visual alert on the report's card
Absence of data (heartbeat) detection
A stateless comparison such as value < threshold
A pipeline Fail activity in the ingestion pipeline

questions.explanation: Activator rules can detect absence of data (heartbeat) through temporal sequencing. A stateless comparison needs an event to arrive, so it can't fire when events stop.

questions.stem: Which two event sources can Fabric Activator monitor to trigger actions? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: An eventstream
The Windows event log on an on-premises gateway machine
The commit history of a Git repository connected to the workspace
The Spark UI's Stages tab of a running notebook
Fabric workspace item events, such as an item being created or deleted

questions.explanation: Activator takes events from eventstreams and from Fabric events such as workspace item events (create, update, delete). Git history, the Spark UI and gateway machine logs aren't Activator sources.
